McLaren.summary: McLaren has tweaked the front wing to smooth the airflow, giving the car a cleaner “bite” into the corners. The rear wing is set to a medium‑downforce configuration, balancing straight‑line speed with enough grip for the track’s sweeping sections. A re‑worked front‑suspension geometry helps the car stay stable under heavy braking, meaning drivers can push later into the turn and extract more lap time this weekend.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has added larger brake‑duct openings on the floor corners, giving the brakes extra cooling so the drivers can push harder through the heavy‑braking sections of this circuit. At the same time they’ve trimmed a small wing piece on the floor edge, cleaning up the airflow under the car for a touch more grip. The two tweaks should let the team run a bit faster and stay in the hunt for podium places this weekend.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has tweaked the front‑corner airflow, fitting a brake duct with a bigger exit to boost cooling on this circuit’s demanding layout. That extra airflow means the brakes stay in the optimal temperature window longer, letting the driver brake harder and later into the corners. In short, more grip off the line and less risk of brake fade right where it counts for the weekend’s battles.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has given the front wing a quick shape‑tweak, shortening the flap to suit this circuit’s high‑speed corners. The change aims to smooth the airflow and give the car a more stable front end, which should improve grip and confidence through the fast turns. In short, a sharper wing means better balance and a better chance to fight for points this weekend.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls have tweaked the front wing for this track, shortening the backmost flap to give the car a more balanced feel through the corners. They’ve also reshaped the tiny winglet on the rear‑corner side pod to smooth the airflow and boost down‑force. Together, the changes should make the car steadier in high‑speed bends and help it stick to the tarmac when it matters most this weekend.
